description: Sign-value table for Linear A. Syllabograms (in 'signs') map to phonetic readings with confidence scores. Logograms (in 'logograms') are commodity ideograms used standalone with quantities, and fractions (in 'fractions') are the A700-series klasmatograms. resolution_summary lists the resolved and proposed values.

K.note: Linear A K-signs neutralize velar voicing and emphasis. KA can represent /ka/, /ga/, or /qa/.

P.note: Labial voicing neutralized. PA can represent /pa/ or /ba/.

T.note: Dental voicing neutralized. TA can represent /ta/ or /da/. Also covers interdentals ṯ/ḏ.

S.note: Sibilant series. SA may represent /sa/, /sha/, or /tsa/. SA-SA digraph = single /sh/.

R.note: Liquid interchange. RA = /ra/ or /la/. RA2 (AB76) specifically marks /la/. JU marks /lu/ (or /la/ in alternate contexts); √d-l-t and √š-l-ṭ show it (DE-JU-KU is a personal name, not √d-l-q).

resolution_summary._note: The resolved sign count. phonemic, logograms and fractions list resolved values only: support independent of a Semitic match (a Linear B value, balancing arithmetic, or a spelling variant of the same word). proposed lists the other values of CANDIDATE or above, with their evidence where it is given; the tier is in the sign's own record. *118.note: Emphatic dental sign, filling the gap between DA and TA in the standard syllabary. DA writes d and TA writes t, as Linear B keeps its D and T series apart (lexicon dental readings: 141 match, 6 mismatch), but no sign writes emphatic /ṭ/, which Semitic languages require. *118 covers emphatic and marked dentals (ṭ, ḍ, ḏ), beside *314 = ḤA in the pharyngeal gap. QA-*118 stands in 5 words, and QA-DA only inside QA-QA-DA (PE2); DA-SI-*118 uses both signs in one word. 26 occurrences across 8 sites. || Standing alone with a quantity (HT12 '*118 5', HT24b ×3 with fractions 1¾/1¾/1, KN2 '*118 3'), *118 is the weight logogram, the talent, as Linear B *118 L (Bartoněk 2003, 126; Killen 2024, 141); the syllabic reading applies only inside words and ligatures. || d is possible only in QA-*118-SA qōdeš 'holy portion' (HT70; HALOT 1076), ṯ in QA-*118 quṯṯāʾ 'cucumber' (HALOT 1151) and *21F-*118 ḥṯ 'unleavened bread' (DULAT 373).

*86.note: Speculative. A mostly standalone sign (16 of 24 tokens) whose syllabic value is undetermined: na leads ro and da by a hair (0.795, 0.769, 0.767), and NA (AB06) and *301 already write na. The emphatic ṇa stays an alternate; no test separates it from na. Syllabic witnesses are few: *86-SI-NI (HT140); *86-RO, *86 on face a and RO on face g of KHWa1013–1016, one scribe; RE-*86 (MILZb4), the second sign incomplete. In *86-SI-*118-KA (HT140) *86 lies in the break. The other tokens are standalone *86 with a numeral or the *86+*188 ligature. (b) standalone JU without quantity, separator-delimited votive context (KNZb4 'JU 𐄁 JA-SI 𐄁 SI') = syllabic /lu/—dedicatory preposition l(u) 'to/for' or asseverative lū, CANDIDATE. (c) word-internal JU = /lu/ or /yu/ (below). *ḳamḥ- 'flour' for KE-JU-MI stays rejected (unaccounted l). || JU writes a palatal liquid, /ʎu/ ~ /lʸu/: lu in Semitic roots (DA-JU-TE, SU-JU-TA), yu where the word needs the glide (KNZc6 JU-KU-NA yukūna, √k-w-n, DULAT 442; the endings -iyyu, -y, KU-RE-JU beside KU-RE; A-RA-JU ʾArāyu = ᵘʳᵘA-ra-yu, RGTC 12/2, 30). It is the u-member of RA₂'s series: Linear B *76 ra₂ = /rya, lya/ and ro₂ = /ryo, lyo/, 'liquid yodized resonants', *76 'already attested in Linear A' (Melena 2014, 63); Linear A had 'a series of post-palatalized and post-labialized consonants' (Palaima 2020, 8). Linear B took JU over as *65, which writes both ju and zu (Melena 2014, 16), and renders Linear A JU words with a glide: ku-ma-ju > ka-ma-jo, qa-ti-ju > qa-ti-ja (Davis 2026, 162–163).

ZU.notes: PROBABLE. /ṯu/ (voiceless interdental + /u/). The evidence is cross-script: (1) A-ZU-RA = ʾAṯrat or ʾAṯirat on KNZc7 incantation bowl—primary anchor; (2) Linear B *79 is zu (Davis 2026, 174 n. 641), with only 3–4 attestations—extreme rarity predicted if value is interdental; (3) Voiceless *ṯ merges with z in no Semitic language (> š, s, ś, t; Kogan 2011, 85–103); z for ṯ is sporadic (Ugar. zd 'breast', KTU 1.23:24, DULAT 983), while *ḏ > z is regular; (4) Complementary distribution confirmed: ZA-SI-ZU (ARKH4b) places ZA and ZU in same word; (5) MA-ZU = maṯu 'child/male' (PS #1702) on HT102—supportive match; (6) Cross-script parallel: Linear B ma-*79 (PY En 74+, PY Eo 276) = same sign sequence, same commodity (grain), same qty (3) as Linear A MA-ZU (HT102); (7) Linear B a-*79 (KN Ap 618+, MY Oe 123) may = PS *ʾanṯ-/ʾaṯt- 'female/woman'—women's personnel + wool contexts. Contexts scored blind run 3:1:17 TH/ZU/neutral; complementary distribution holds on 18 of 32 tablets; onomastic parallels run 4:3 TH/ZU. KU-ZU-NI = Ugaritic PN Kuṯinu/Kṯn (DULAT p.467; syllabic vocalization ku-ši-nu, PRU 3 195, UVST 231). ZU-DI-RA = /ṯudira/ (Ugaritic ṯdr 'waitress/girl', Hurro-Hittite loan from šiduri; contact layer). Phonetic range note: ZU covers [θ ~ s̪] zone (native NWS /ṯ/ and borrowed Hurrian /š/ both render as ṯ in Ugaritic orthography), not a point value. || ZU writes the interdental range, ṯ, ḏ and ṯ̣, before every vowel, as Old Babylonian PI writes wa, we, wi and wu (Huehnergard 2011, 69), and as the u-member of the Z-row zu as well, as SA writes s and š. ṯ reads A-ZU-RA, MA-ZU, ZU-DI-RA, ZU-RI-NI-MA, DU-ZU-WA, KU-ZU-NI and ZU-JU-PU₂; z reads RU-ZU-NA rāzin 'dignitary' (Heb. rōzēn, HALOT 1210; Ar. razuna, Lane 1079, PS *z); ZU-DU and ZU-DI read 'breast' under both (ṯd, zd: DULAT 886, 983). Linear B *79 stands in the z-row.

AU.notes: Diphthong sign /aw/, not a standard CV syllabogram, from the Linear B grid correspondence (B85 au). Dual function: syllabic /aw/ in AU-RE-TE = ʾawrēt 'luminous one' (√ʾ-w-r, KH6) and SE-WA-AU-DE (ZAZg35), and AU after the divider that follows A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA on IOZa3; the pig logogram SUS at HT38 and HT118, and with SI set above it on PH(?)31a.3 and b.4. AU-TA in KO(?)Zf2 is excluded as confirmation because that inscription has no word dividers. The /aw/ diphthong is productive in archaic NWS (*ʾawr 'light', *ʾawt 'sign', *ṯawr 'bull') and monophthongizes to /ō/ in later Canaanite. Cross-syllabary parallel: Linear B a₃ (AB16) = /ai/, a dedicated diphthong sign for word-initial /ai/ (Judson 2016; Palaima 2018)—the daughter script retains a non-CV sign where Greek requires one, just as Linear A has AU=/aw/ where NWS requires one. Skeleton-search convention for AU-bearing words: run the tool default (AU → w) and check two variants—(b) ʾ-transparent (AU → ʾw, initial ʾ dropping word-initially), (c) monophthong (AU → vowel only, no consonant contribution); report which variant any claimed match rests on. *310.note: VC (vowel-consonant) sign /in/, NOT a standard CV syllabogram. Structural parallel to AU=/aw/: both are VC signs that close syllables rather than open them. IN handles the coda /n/ in closed syllables: QA-IN-I = /qayn-ī/ (where IN provides the syllable-closing /n/ that standard NI cannot). The script has at least two VC signs (AU=/aw/, *310=/in/) alongside its CV core, reflecting adaptation for Semitic closed-syllable morphology. 10 occurrences across Haghia Triada, Knossos, Zakros. KI-IN-RE = kinnare is the anchor reading—the ancient lyre, cognate with Hebrew kinnōr.

logograms._note: Commodity ideograms—standalone signs paired with quantities to denote goods. Classified separately from syllabograms. Some signs have rare word-embedded occurrences that may indicate acrophonic syllabographic potential. Gendered livestock system: *21F/M=sheep, *22F/M=goat, *23M=cattle.

Hebrew ʿanāqā, Arabic ʿanāq, Syriac ʿnaqqā
Hebrew gᵉdī, Arabic jady, Akkadian gadû

*22F.note_male_terms: *tayš- (he-goat), *ʿat(t)ūd- (he-goat) excluded—inapplicable to female-marked logogram. No d-q root for goat exists in any Semitic branch (Starling DB, Tsammalex confirmed).

rebus_hypothesis.principle: Rebus extraction from the final syllable of a Semitic name, comparable to the still-candidate *49/TAMIR hypothesis (ta-MI-r → /mi/). PS *ʿanz- is sibilant *z (confirmed, not interdental *ḏ). Akkadian enzu syllabified in Linear A CV script: E-NI-ZU. Final syllable → /zu/.
rebus_hypothesis.gap_filled: Would fill /zu/ gap created by ZU (AB79) revaluation to /ṯu/.
rebus_hypothesis.test_case: ZU-*22F-DI on HT101 (commodity allocation, Haghia Triada). If *22F=/zu/ and ZU=/du/ (T-class neutralization): du-zu-dī. Inconclusive—could be PN, toponym, or opaque.
rebus_hypothesis.supersedes: Acrophonic /ʿe/ (from *ʿēz) and /ʿa/ (from *ʿanz-)—weaker because they duplicate *306=/ʿa/ territory; the proposed TAMIR comparison is supporting analogy, not independent proof.

*22F.syllabogram_exclusion_note: AB22 (CAP) was listed among 6 'unresolved standard syllabograms' but functions purely as a commodity logogram in Linear A. 14× standalone *22F, 5× standalone CAP, 3× standalone *22M, with only 1 embedded occurrence (ZU-*22F-DI on HT101 — possible acrophonic rebus /ʿe/). Linear B also uses AB22 as an ideogram (CAPf/CAPm), not a syllabogram. Formally excluded from unresolved syllabogram count.

*21M.note: Male sheep logogram. Part of gendered livestock pair (*21F=ewe/OVISf, *21M=ram/OVISm). WARNING: *21F in the 'signs' section is the /ha/ syllabogram—different physical sign, AB number collision.

*22M.syllabogram_exclusion_note: See *22F note. AB22 functions as commodity logogram pair (*22F=CAPf, *22M=CAPm), not a syllabogram.

*23M.gloss: young bull, head of cattle (live livestock)
*23M.semitic_term: *mūru (PS *muhr- / *mVrVʔ- √m-r-ʾ), Akkadian mūru 'foal; calf' (OAkk. on, CAD M2 229), mīru 'young bull' (OB-SB, CAD M2 109), Ugaritic mru, Hebrew mǝrīʾ 'fatted steer'
*23M.note: Live head-count logogram: whole numbers only (1-5), never fractions. Complementary to TU = ṯawr 'cattle products' (fractional quantities: 1/16, 1/4, 3/4). Zero tablet overlap between *23M and TU. MU = /mu/ spells mūru's /ū/; mūru keeps its calf sense through Middle and Neo-Assyrian (CAD M2 229–30), so no equine/bovine split is needed. The MU (AB23) base sign abbreviates the onset syllable /mu/ of *mūru.

*401.semitic_term: *rVqVḥ- (PS S15), Akkadian ruqqû/rāqiḫu, Hebrew rōqēaḥ/riqqūḥīm, Ugaritic rqḥ/mrqḥt, Phoenician rqḥ
*401.note: Never standalone—always appears with phonetic complement (+RU, +RO) or compound modifier (+*304). +RU = ruqqû "perfumed/refined oil" (initial ru-); +RO = rōqēaḥ "compounded ointment" (initial rō-). Both subtypes on KH91 prove distinct products. +*304(pidru) = fat-based aromatic. Co-occurs with CYP, OLE, *308(šamnu), *304(pidru) in aromatic/oil register. Fractional quantities (¹⁄₅, ¹⁄₁₆). 13/15 at Khania. Mutation testing: INERT/CONTEXTUAL_MARK = non-syllabic confirmed.

contexts: HT132: after A-SE and before quantity 5
A319.note: A319 is the standard designation; *904 is a legacy alias. Never initial or medial in a word: it closes MA-TI-TI (HT Zd 155, 157) or stands before a number (HT 132.1 A319 5; HT Zd 156 A319 2¼, A319 3⅜). A logogram with no sound value, on HT 132 'a probable transaction sign' (Steele 2024, 103). Not *171 (curved top, stem crossbar, forked foot) and not Linear B T (no fractions). Cretan Hieroglyphic comparandum CH 065 (Meissner & Salgarella in Civitillo, Ferrara & Meissner 2024, Table 7.2, p. 152).

*307.note: Value from a spelling variant: JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-*307-PU₂-RE (PK Za 8) and JA-DI-KI-TE-TE-DU-PU₂-RE (PK Za 15), *307 in the place of DU. 8/0/0 inscription test (0 LESS READABLE). Forms: VIR+*307 (sanctuary personnel; KH 9, 14, 19), OLE *307 1½ (PE Wy 5, two signs), KU-RO *307 156 (HT 127b), and *307 doubled (A 638) heading the personnel lists HT 85a and HT 97a and HT 36. Montecchi 2008, 315–16 reads A 307 as a transaction sign for distributing rations or payments, A 638 its doubled variant; Uchitel 2006, 75–76 as a general qualification of personnel groups.

*304.note: +PA complement (6×) confirms /pa/ initial. Commodity ideogram in oil register between OLE and OLIV. || SUSPENDED: the HT82 three-way conflict (transliteratedWords says *304+[ ], the tablet's own glyph is A628 not A653, SigLA reads the position as A653=*401+*304 ligature — a different sign) shows the PIDRU reading rested on the siglum, not the glyph. *304 is read by glyph. The commodity/gloss/root/semitic_term below are the retired PIDRU hypothesis, kept for reference; not an active reading until a facsimile check of the A653/A628 mismatch.

*49.gloss: palm/tree or palm produce; TAMIR and phonetic /mi/ are candidate identifications
*49.note: Semantic reading: PALM/TREE, based on the pictorial form and counted administrative contexts. TAMIR is the proposed Semitic lexical name, and /mi/ its proposed syllabic use. Both are speculative: TO-*49-RE yields t-m-r only after /mi/ is assumed, while Linear B tu-*49-mi places *49 beside ordinary MI. Dawmi for HT120 is a contingent name reading.

*188.note: High frequency (29×). Compound forms: SU-PU₂-*188 (jar of terebinth), PA₃-*188 (phonetic complement), *188-*308 (terebinth oil).

*308.note: Oil derivative modifier. Appears in compound *188-*308 (terebinth oil). HT123+124a converts OLIV into *308 at about one quarter in four parallel entries (31 → 8 ¹⁄₄, 31 ¹⁄₂ → 8 ³⁄₄, 16 → 4, 15 → 4 ¹⁄₄). Word proposed: šamnu (√š-m-n; PS *šamn-, Akkadian šamnu, Hebrew šemen), which OLE also carries.

*301.rebus_hypothesis: *301 logogram yields phonetic /na/ from initial radical of √n-w-y. Logograms can represent any sound within their source word.
embedded_contexts: A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA (libation formula verb, 11 att., 5 peak sanctuary sites)
A-NA-TI-*301-WA-JA (IOZa8; ʿAnatī nawaya 'my Anat, my abode', √n-w-y noun)
*301.note: Core logogram of the peak sanctuary libation formula. 288 total occurrences across 16 sites (256 standalone, 32 embedded). Root √n-w-y "to dwell, settle"—the libation verb A-TA-I-*301-WA-JA = ʾata-inawaya "I make myself a dwelling" is CONFIRMED across 5 peak sanctuary sites. Independent noun *301-WA = nawa "dwelling" at IOZa4. Phonetic value /na/ derived from initial radical. Compare the candidate *49 PALM/TREE → TAMIR → /mi/ hypothesis and the stronger *307=DUBUR complement pattern.

*317.semitic_term: Akkadian liqtu, Ugaritic lqḥ, Hebrew miqqāḥ
*317.note: 5 occurrences across 4 tablets (3 sites). JU+*317+QE on HT89 brackets with /lu/+/qe/ yielding l-...-q frame.

*305.note: Dual-function: logogram (60%, standalone with quantities 1-90) + syllabogram /da/ (40%, word-embedded). Acrophonic: /da/ → √d-b-ḥ → dabbāḥū. || The logographic reading *305 = DABBĀḤŪ 'sacrificers' stands at PROBABLE 0.75, as in the lexicon; the syllabic value /ḏa/ is speculative.

*516.note: Administrative logogram. √s-p-r "to count, record"—Hebrew sēper/sōpēr "book/scribe", Akkadian šipru "sending, message". Phonetic complement SI- confirms initial /s/.

*312.gloss: flax/linen (√k-t-n); inside a word it writes KI, the first syllable of kitnu
*312.semitic_term: *kitn- (PS), Ugaritic ktn, Akkadian kitû, Hebrew kuttōnet, Greek χιτών (loanword)
*312.rebus_hypothesis: KI (acrophonic, first syllable of kitnu)—*312-TE-TE = KI-TE-TE kitītu on HT26a; SPECULATIVE
*312.note: 9 corpus contexts: 4 standalone (HT49a, HT123+124b, KH8, ARKH3a), 4 in words (*312-TA, *312-TE-TE, MU-*312, *312-TA₂), 1 compound (TELA+*312, HT38), which ties the sign to cloth. KI-TA-NA 'linen' is spelled out on PEZb3. In *312-TE-TE (HT26a) the logogram writes KI, the first syllable of kitnu, as *307 writes DU in *307-PU₂-RE: KI-TE-TE = Akk. kitītu (CAD K 466). Standard KI beside standalone *312 on HT49a does not block this, since *312 stands for its syllable only inside a word. ZA6b *312-TA₂ GRA+PA 40 is an entry receiving grain, set out like I-KU-JU-TI-*28B GRA+PA 50¼ above it, not a grain heading. MU-*312 (HT78) stands alone on a fragment. Alternative: MANÛ 'measure/portion' (√m-n-y).

*406VAS.semitic_term: *kaʾs- (PS #297), Akkadian kāsu, Hebrew kōs, Arabic kaʾs
*406VAS.note: Pictographic vessel ideogram. Always appears with +KE phonetic complement on HT26 (both sides, as tablet header). Bare form *406-VS on HT93a (alongside DA-RI-DA, qty 2). KE complement indicates initial syllable of vessel word: PS *kaʾs- "vessel for beer, bowl" → NWS *kēs (vowel fronting from medial aleph) → KE. KA-SI on HTWa1027 nodule may be the syllabic spelling of the same word (skeleton k-s, distance 0.000).

*412.gloss: bowl, basin (large open vessel for liquids)
*412.semitic_term: *ʔigān- (PS #1358), Akkadian agannu, Hebrew ʔaggān, Arabic ʔiggānat-
*412.note: Commodity ideogram on MA10 4-sided bar (all 4 faces) alongside *413+SU, *405+Ω, *402+A, *414+F—a catalog of complemented ideograms. PS *ʔigān- 'cup, bowl': Arabic preserves /i/-class vowel (ʔiggānat-); NWS /i/→/ē/ lowering yields /ʔēgān/; aleph drops → complement E = /ʔē-/. Hebrew shifted to /a/ (ʔaggān, Exod 24:6, Song 7:3, Isa 22:24). PH9b *412-VS-VIN = wine bowl. Distinct from *406VAS=KĀS (cup)—ʔaggān is larger basin type. TI+*412VAS = subtype (TI prefix, cf. Linear B variety marking).

*316.gloss: bean, legume (food commodity in ration allocations)
*316.note: Commodity ideogram *316 (6 att., Khania + Phaistos). KI complement on nodules KHWa1001/1002 gives initial syllable /ki/. On KH91, positioned between VIN (wine) and NI (figs) in a rations list alongside GRA and *401+RU/RO—food commodity context. On PH1a, allocated to named individuals with CYP. Akkadian kiššanu 'bean' (CAD K 454); no Hebrew or Ugaritic reflexes confirmed.

SI+SE.gloss: administrative entity or category; speculative comparison with Ugaritic Šapšu
SI+SE.note: The exact standalone ligature occurs on HT116a and HT42+59 as a quantified administrative entity or category. The expanded forms SI+SE-NI and SI+SE-RA+KA are separate morphological evidence and do not prove a standalone logographic value. Ugaritic Šapšu remains a speculative comparison, because the proposed outer-consonant abbreviation š…š omits medial /p/ and is not independently established for SI+SE. Oil allocations do not by themselves identify a solar deity or cultic context.

semitic_terms.reflexes: Hebrew ḥemʾā (Gen 18:8, Deut 32:14, Judg 5:25, Isa 7:15), Ugaritic ḥmʾt (KTU 1.4 III), Akkadian ḫimētu (palace ration lists, Ur III–NB), Arabic ḥamʾa
semitic_terms.phonology: Initial ḥ drops (guttural dropping) → /emʾat/ → E as logographic abbreviation

E.note: Pure vowel sign — no consonant skeleton, so standard root-matching inapplicable. Identified via distributional analysis: 80% numeral-following (8/10), 3 sites (HT, KN, ZA), late position in oil-heavy commodity sequences. Cross-commodity modifier (CYP+E, OLE+E, GRA+E) consistent with dairy fat as parallel fat category to olive oil. Cognate attested across all major Semitic branches. Deut 32:14 ḥemʾat bāqār is the exact construct form this logogram would abbreviate. Clarified butter (ghee) is the natural stored dairy commodity in warm-climate palace economies.

TI.semitic_term: *tiʔin- (PS SED I #260), Akkadian tittu/tiʔittu/tīnātu, Ugaritic tʔn, Hebrew tǝʔēnā, Arabic tīn-, Phoenician (unvocalized)
TI.note: Dual-function sign: syllabogram /ti/ (AB04) + logogram TIʔIN when standalone with quantities. Abbreviation of TI-NI = tiʔin 'figs' (CANDIDATE, lexicon). 12 standalone across 11 tablets, 6 sites. 58% followed by numerals. Quantities: ¼, 1, 2, 7, 13, 13, 100. Key evidence: ZA12a/b commodity cluster (TI 13 on both faces alongside PA and RU); PH30 fractional quantity (TI ¼); HT154 bulk quantity (*516 TI 100). Pan-Semitic *tiʔin- attestation (Akk, Ug, Heb, Ar, Phoen) confirms figs as inherited core vocabulary. Appears in Deut 8:8 Seven Species. Pictographic evidence absent (AB04 is not botanical), but the TI-NI compound provides the semantic anchor.

QE.gloss: measure unit (qê, Akkadian genitive of qû ≈ 1.2 liters)
QE.semitic_term: PS *qab(b)- → Akkadian qû (CAD Q 294), gen. qê; Hebrew qab (HALOT 1060, 2 Kgs 6:25)
QE.rebus_hypothesis: Metrological logogram borrowed from Akkadian administrative register. Akkadian gen. form qê is the construct-chain form heard in ration texts ("5 qê šamni" = "5 measures of oil"). Functions both as standalone logogram (QE + numeral) and as bound suffix on commodity nouns (NOUN-QE = "a qê-measure of NOUN").
QE.note: Dual-function sign: syllabogram /qe/ (AB78) + metrological logogram QÊ when standalone or suffixed to commodity nouns. 7 standalone across 5 tablets (4 sites), always followed by numerals (3, 17, 21, 30). 8 suffix attestations on 7 distinct words. Key evidence: HTWc3014 roundel KU-MI-NA-QE + CAP = "a measure of cumin + goats" (commodity transaction tag). Suffixal behavior distinguishes QÊ from other commodity logograms — it modifies the preceding noun rather than standing alone as a commodity category. PS *qab(b)- "dry/liquid measure" (Starling #2827, domain: Metrology).

VIN+WA phonetic complement (HT27b); pan-Semitic *wayn-. Independently validated by Salgarella 2022 (Mix and Match): confirms VIN+WA as phonetic complement and proposes Minoan word for wine began with /wa/, consistent with Semitic *wayn-.
*308 = ŠAMNU (pressed oil derivative) confirms š-m-n root; 18 compound sub-types; pan-Semitic *šamnu
OLIV distinct from OLE (fruit vs oil) on same tablets; HT123+124a olive processing; pan-Semitic *zayt

logographic_value.meaning: plant root (base logogram in composite signs, never attested independently)
logographic_value.evidence: Salgarella et al. 2025: lower S-shaped element shared by LA A646 and LB *157. Functions as base logogram for 'root' in composites. Acrophonic principle: upper syllabogram abbreviates commodity word.

logographic_value.meaning: root commodity (spice/root product); acrophonic PI indicates Minoan word for 'root' began with /pi/
logographic_value.evidence: Salgarella et al. 2025, HT 33: composite of A341 (RADix base) + PI (upper syllabogram). LB parallel *157 = A341 + AB40/wi (abbreviating wi-ri-za 'root'). LA uses PI instead, indexing the Minoan word.

Salgarella 2022 (Mix and Match): A559 = MA+RU composite. Bottom-up reading (biggest sign = MA, then RU). The same ligature is the Linear B wool logogram *145 LANA. Nosch & Weilhartner 2026 confirm wool logogram. 9 tokens: HT12, HT24a (×4), KH43, PH3a, THE8.

*131B.gloss: must/new wine (unfermented or partially fermented grape juice)
*131B.note: Wine-variant logogram. AB131 family: VIN (AB131) = wine (*wayn*), *131B = must (*tirōšu*), *131C = vinegar (ACETUM). 4 attestations: ARKH2, ARKH3a, ARKH5, ZA10b. Consistently paired with quantities in allocation lists alongside GRA and OLIV, mirroring the biblical dāgān-tīrōš-yiṣhār triad (Deut 7:13). Modest quantities (2–6 units) fit must as a less-abundant commodity than standard wine. Recurs in the Arkhanes ration formula (recipient + GRA/*131B + quantity): ARKH2 and ARKH5, beside GRA on ARKH5. No syllabic spelling of the word is known, and Ugaritic has trṯ, not trš. Rival: SigLA codes all four tokens VINb, a variant of VIN.

*322.semitic_term: *pir- (PS #756), Hebrew pǝrī, Ugaritic pr, Phoenician pr, Arabic θamar (semantic parallel)
*322.note: 3× standalone on Khania roundels (KHWc2026, KHWc2027, KHWc2098) = commodity logogram behavior. 1× syllabic *322-RI on HT11a = phonetic complement confirming word ends in /-ri/. PS *pir- 'fruit' (Hebrew pǝrī, Ugaritic pr) is the strongest NWS commodity ending in -rī. Compare DUBUR and BUṬNU; *49 PALM/TREE → TAMIR is only a candidate parallel. HT11a context: land-allocation tablet alongside A-RU-RA 'arable land' and KA-RO-NA 'horn'—fruit fits agricultural allocation.

*309.gloss: round (loaf/disc/talent-weight); on TY2 most plausibly bread-rounds in ration quantities
*309.semitic_term: Hebrew kikkār 'round loaf, talent, disc' (kikkar leḥem Exod 29:23, 1 Sam 2:36); Akkadian kakkaru; Ugaritic kkr 'talent'
compound_forms: *309-DA-PU-[?] (10; lost sign after PU, GORILA I 325)
*309-RU-JU-KI (100, after PA-DA; RU written on top of *309, GORILA I 325)
*309C-[?]-RU-KA (30; AB53 hook on top of *309C unread, GORILA I 325)
*309.note: Circle-based sign family, site-unique to TY2 (11 tokens): plain circle = *309, interior-marked variants = *309B/*309C (SigLA drawing). Pictograph matches the word's core sense—kikkār is 'a round.' Phonetic-spelling anchor: KE-KI-RU = kikkaru PROBABLE 0.7 at HT94b. B carries the largest counts (500, 250); C takes 17[ ] and 30, but plain *309 takes the smallest counts (10, 6), so the variants are not a size grade on this evidence. Ration arithmetic sane: Σ*309 = 1,413 rounds (1,333 if line 5 reads 80) vs VIR+[?] 84 ≈ 17 per man; as metal talents 500 units ≈ 15 tons, implausible at Tylissos. Suffix strings form two families (-PU set: *34-PU-PI/KI-PU/DA-PU; -JU set: JU-KI/RI-JU/DA-[?]-JU/[?]-WA-JU), qualifiers unresolved. Prior v3 phonetic solver: no signal.

embedded_contexts: word-internal = syllabic ṬA (speculative); a dual-function sign, read by position
*118.note: Standalone arm only: after a commodity sign and before a numeral (HT12 wool, HT24b ×3 with 1¾, HT38, KN2), the talent, as Linear B *118 L (Bartoněk 2003, 126; Killen 2024, 141). HT24b totals 4½; the recto wool total, restored as 45, gives the Linear B ratio of 10 to the talent (Del Freo 2020, 56).
